mechanism_narrative: The workplace series jumped from -31.0 at t-2w to -17.6 at t-0w and has held that level for two weeks, which means commuting routines are being re-established. Restored weekday footfall traffic lifts retail-and-recreation mobility over the following four weeks, so mean RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -31.0 at t-2w to -17.6 at t-0w and stayed near -17
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below its last-28-day mean in more than 50% of weeks where WORKPLACES sits 10 or more points above its four-week low.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has drifted down from 15.0 at t-2w to 12.1 at t-0w, the lowest reading in the window, so a growing share of the population is spending time outside the home. Each step down in time-at-home substitutes into out-of-home discretionary trips, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined in three of the last four weeks, reaching 12.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is flat or lower while RESIDENTIAL continues to fall week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS collapsed from -22.4 at t-1w to -28.1 at t-0w, a single-week drop of 5.7 points into the deepest reading of the window. A parks break of that size marks withdrawal of outdoor discretionary activity, which co-moves with retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC falls over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points week-on-week (t-1w -22.4 to t-0w -28.1)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 5.7 points from t-1w to t-0w, its lowest value in the window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean whenever PARKS prints a week-on-week decline larger than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of WORKPLACES recovering to -17.6 while RESIDENTIAL falls to 12.1 is only jointly consistent with genuine return to pre-pandemic routines; neither series alone is informative. When both move together, discretionary retail traffic follows within four weeks and RETAIL_REC rises.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises at least 5 points versus t-2w while RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point versus t-2w
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 13.4 points and RESIDENTIAL fell 2.9 points between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean when WORKPLACES is at least 5 points above its t-2w value and RESIDENTIAL is below its t-2w value in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has been pinned within a 1.7-point band (-25.3 to -27.1) for four straight weeks, which is the signature of a fixed capacity restriction rather than voluntary avoidance. A binding transit cap keeps non-essential trips suppressed, so RETAIL_REC stays below its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -25.3 and -27.1 across all four weeks
regime_hint: steady-state partial restrictions with capped transit capacity
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT remains inside a 2-point band around -26.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM sits 22 to 28 points above baseline in every week of the window, indicating that household provisioning is still being run through grocery channels instead of restaurants and leisure venues. Sustained grocery substitution crowds out retail-and-recreation spend, holding RETAIL_REC below its trailing mean for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above +20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM held between 22.0 and 27.6 in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean in more than half of weeks where GROCERY_PHARM remains above +20.

mechanism_narrative: The mid-January window is the post-holiday trough: PARKS fell to -28.1 and RETAIL_REC slid to -27.9, its lowest reading in the window. Seasonality keeps discretionary footfall depressed through the next week before any recovery, so the one-week-ahead RETAIL_REC mean is below the trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically from -26.3 at t-3w to -27.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: The one-week-ahead RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the trailing four-week mean in years or windows matching this mid-January date.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS at -28.1 and TRANSIT flat at -25.4 together show discretionary trip-making is being cut at both the outdoor and the transit margin while the commute level is unchanged. The combination squeezes non-commute retail trips, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is at least 5 points below its four-week mean while TRANSIT is within 2 points of its four-week mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -28.1 while TRANSIT held at -25.4 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is above its last-28-day mean in weeks where PARKS is more than 5 points below its four-week mean and TRANSIT is within 2 points of its four-week mean.
